Everything, one hover away. 
Point at the top of the screen and the notch opens. Every clip is a real recording. 
Music, without switching apps. 
See what’s playing, skip a track or pause, and switch speakers. 
Video: The notch music player skips from one song to the next. 
Drag files up. 
Drag a file to the top of the screen. Drop it in the Tray and it waits for you in the notch, or AirDrop it in one move. 
Video: A folder is dragged to the notch, which shows AirDrop and Tray. It lands in the Tray. 
Downloads, in view. 
Progress fills the notch while a file downloads, so you know when it’s done without opening your browser. 
Video: The notch shows a file download counting up to 100 percent. 
Convert files in place. 
Pick a file, pick a format. PNG, JPEG, HEIC, PDF, ZIP and more, right in the notch. 
Video: The file converter changes an image to ZIP and shows a green check. 
A timer you can see. 
Set it on the ruler and start. The countdown stays at the top of your screen while you work. 
Video: A 15 minute timer starts and counts down in the notch. 
Type it. Get reminded. 
Write what to remember and when, like “in 30m”. NotchMind reminds you on time. 
Video: A reminder is typed with in 30m and added to the list. 
Weather, at a glance. 
Today and the next few days, in °F or °C. No app, no tab. 
Video: The weather page for Surat switches from Fahrenheit to Celsius. 
Pick your finish 
Liquid Glass, in your notch. 
The notch refracts your wallpaper, just like the rest of macOS. Or keep it black. Change it any time in Settings.

Colors, JSON, links and commands get the right tools. Passwords get cleared. All on your Mac. 
It knows what you copied. 
Copy a color and get tools to preview and convert it. Copy JSON and format it in one click. Links, emails, paths and commands work too. All recognized on your Mac. 
Video: The notch recognizes a copied color and valid JSON and offers actions for each. 
And keeps secrets secret. 
Copy a password or an API key and Secret Guard keeps it on your Mac and clears it in a tap. 
Video: A copied API key triggers a red Possible secret copied card; Clear Clipboard removes it.

The little things, noticed. 
Plug in, connect your AirPods, change the volume. The notch shows it for a moment, then gets out of the way. 
Plugged in. 
Connect power and see your battery level. 
Video: The notch widens to show Plugged In at 100 percent. 
AirPods, connected. 
Your headphones and their battery, the moment they connect. 
Video: The notch shows headphones connected with 10 percent battery. 
Volume, up top. 
Changes show in the notch, not over your work. 
Video: The notch shows a volume level bar. 
Drives, spotted. 
Plug in a drive and eject it from the notch. 
Video: A drive called Photos Backup appears with an eject button. 
CPU and memory. 
Live graphs of how hard your Mac is working. 
Video: CPU and RAM cards with live graphs. 
Your AI usage. 
Tokens used by Codex and Claude Code, today and this month. 
Video: Claude Code usage: 2.83 million tokens in 30 days. 
Dev tools. 
Format JSON, encode Base64 and URLs, make UUIDs. 
Video: The developer tools page with a Format JSON box.

## Building weird, useful things  
and shipping them fast.
I’m Rudra — a GenAI engineer and indie builder from Surat. I build AI agents, the tooling that evaluates them, and small apps that make a computer feel a little more fun to use.
> A demo is a promise. Shipping is keeping it.
Builder Red-teamer Mac nerd Learner
Location
Surat, India
Studying
B.Tech AI & ML · ’26
Focus
Agents · Evals · Mac apps
## How it started
I’ve been on GitHub since 2020, mostly breaking things to see how they work. In 2022 I started a B.Tech in Computer Science (AI & ML) at P. P. Savani University — deep learning, computer vision, databases, and a lot of late-night side projects.
Certifications along the way pulled me in different directions: neural networks with DeepLearning.AI, quantum algorithms with CU Boulder, and networking and security with Google. The security bit stuck.
## Where it’s going
Now I spend most of my time on LLM evaluation and red teaming. cot-redteam-agent, my open-source CLI on PyPI, is built on one stubborn rule: a refusal that quotes the secret is not a leak — only real disclosure or observed tool impact counts.
On the other side of the brain, I make indie software. NotchMind turns the MacBook notch into a little home for your day. TapNoise gives your Mac the sound of a dream keyboard, plus Tappy — the keycap following your cursor right now. AuraFarm and TestMyGear live on the web, and vibe-learn teaches you while Claude Code writes.
## How I work
*   01
Proof over vibes
If a metric can be gamed, it will be. I’d rather count observed behaviour than trust a judge’s opinion.
*   02
Local by default
NotchMind, TapNoise and TestMyGear do their work on your device. Your clipboard and keystrokes are none of my business.
*   03
Fun first, then useful
Software can make you smile and still do real work. Tappy is proof.
*   04
Ship, then sharpen
Six products out the door taught me more than any perfect plan would have.
## Journey
1.   2020 Joined GitHub
Started pushing code and breaking things in public. 
2.   2022 B.Tech, CSE (AI & ML)
P. P. Savani University — AI, deep learning, databases, computer vision. 
3.   Jun 2026[vibe-learn A Claude Code skill that teaches while you vibe code.](http://rudrasatani.com/projects/vibe-learn)
4.   Jul 2026[cot-redteam-agent on PyPI Open-source LLM red-teaming CLI — now at v0.6 with a proof-of-action agent lane.](http://rudrasatani.com/projects/cot-redteam-agent)
5.   2026[AuraFarm & TestMyGear go live A group-chat judging game and a browser hardware lab.](http://rudrasatani.com/projects/aurafarm)
6.   2026[NotchMind & TapNoise for Mac Two paid, native macOS apps — the notch and the keyboard, made fun.](http://rudrasatani.com/projects/notchmind)
7.   Next HelloOrbita, samegrid, gitasaar
iOS widgets, a daily shared puzzle, and a Bhagavad Gita app.

Type softly, it whispers. Hit hard, it clacks.

# 🎓 vibe-learn **Learn while you vibe code.** A [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) skill that turns "the AI wrote it, I don't know how" into "I shipped it *and* I understand it." After meaningful code (or a real bug fix), Claude surfaces **major concepts**, optional **mental models**, and **non-blocking quizzes** — with recap, spaced review, and cross-session progress so it still sticks tomorrow. [](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills) [](./LICENSE) [](./CHANGELOG.md)
[▶ Watch the 16-second demo](https://github.com/rudrasatani13/vibe-learn/releases/download/v1.3.0/vibe-learn-demo.mp4)
--- ## The problem Vibe coding is fast, but it has a cost: you end up with a working app you can't explain. The code becomes a black box, and you don't grow as a developer. The usual fixes are all-or-nothing — either you stop and read docs (kills the flow), or you ship blind (kills the learning). **vibe-learn** sits in the middle. It rides *alongside* the build. Claude Code is the primary supported runtime; the package intentionally uses Claude Code skill and hook extensions: - After a **meaningful** change → short **🎓 Learn** block (2–4 takeaways, jargon from scratch). - After a **real bug fix** → **🐛 Bug class** (root cause, fix idea, prevention). - After a **feature slice** → **🧠 Mental model** (how the pieces connect + failure points). - At natural pauses → **📝 Quick check**, **🔮 Predict**, or **🎤 Interview** questions — all **non-blocking**. - Across sessions → canonical **`.vibe-learn/state.json`**, generated **`.vibe-learn/progress.md`**, and **`/vibe-learn review`** (spaced repetition). - When ready to practice → bounded **`/vibe-learn challenge`** and explain-it-yourself **`/vibe-learn teach-back`**. - End of day → **`/vibe-learn recap`**. - Track momentum → **`/vibe-learn stats`** (streak, mastered, due) and a gentle *welcome back* nudge after a break. - Take it offline → **`/vibe-learn export`** to Anki, CSV, or Markdown flashcards. It changes *nothing* about how the code itself gets written. It only adds teaching around

# CoT Red Team Agent
[](https://github.com/rudrasatani13/cot-redteam-agent/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[](https://pypi.org/project/cot-redteam-agent/)
[](https://www.python.org/)
[](LICENSE)
**Refusal quotes of a canary are not a finding.** This CLI scores *visible*
chain-of-thought and proves simulated-agent impact from observed actions — not
from assistant prose or an LLM judge.
```bash
python -m pip install cot-redteam-agent
```
Published on PyPI as [`cot-redteam-agent`](https://pypi.org/project/cot-redteam-agent/).
## Try it in 30 seconds (no API key)
The keyless `mock` provider never touches the network. The config below is also
shipped as [`cot_redteam/data/mock_demo.example.yaml`](cot_redteam/data/mock_demo.example.yaml).
`mock_mode: auto` discloses a synthetic canary, so `scan` should exit `1`
(findings). That is the demo working — not a real-model vulnerability.
```bash
cat > demo.yaml <<'EOF'
version: 2
global:
  seed: 1
  output_dir: ./results-demo
  concurrency: 1
providers:
  mock:
    kind: mock
    mock_mode: auto
evaluation:
  models:
    - mock:target
  dataset_path: pkg:sample.jsonl
  sample_count: 1
  budgets:
    max_requests: 40
    max_elapsed_seconds: 120
  retain_prompts: false
  retain_responses: false
storage:
  path: ./results-demo/cot_redteam.db
EOF
cot-redteam scan --config demo.yaml
```
Exit codes: `0` clean, `1` findings, `2` config/env, `3` partial. Gate CI on
`1`. Switch `mock_mode` to `refuse` for a clean pass — packaged variants
[`mock_refuse.example.yaml`](cot_redteam/data/mock_refuse.example.yaml) and
[`mock_disclose.example.yaml`](cot_redteam/data/mock_disclose.example.yaml)
sit next to the auto demo. `cot-redteam init --demo mock` writes this keyless
config instead of the OpenRouter example. From a clone, the v0.6 agent lane is
also keyless:
`cot-redteam agent scan --config cot_redteam/data/agent_security.example.yaml`.

Pick the tool that matches the job. This project does not replace a broad
scanner, an orchestration SDK, or a YAML eval harness.

# CubbyPad
**Download:** [CubbyPad.dmg](https://github.com/rudrasatani13/cubbypad-updates/releases/download/updates/CubbyPad.dmg) (the latest version, for macOS 26 or later).
CubbyPad brings back Launchpad: a full-screen grid of your apps, with folders, search, and the F4 key, a hot corner or a trackpad pinch to open it.
### Opening it the first time
macOS says "Apple could not verify CubbyPad" the first time. That's because CubbyPad is an independent app that isn't distributed through Apple. To open it:
1. Open the DMG, drag CubbyPad to Applications, then open it. Click **Done** on the message.
2. Open **System Settings › Privacy & Security**, scroll down, and click **Open Anyway** next to CubbyPad.
3. Confirm with **Open Anyway**.
You only do this once. CubbyPad updates itself after that, with no warning.
